title: Dynamic Positional Attention Modulation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

problem.claim: Uniform adaptation can be suboptimal because attention representations exhibit non-uniform behavior and positional encodings induce dimension-dependent positional structure.

gap.claim: Existing PEFT methods generally do not account for structured heterogeneity across attention dimensions, heads, layers, and input tokens.

contributions.claim: DyPAM is a PEFT method that adapts the contribution of positional information to attention by operating directly on query and key representations.
DyPAM combines input-conditioned, dimension-wise modulation with head-wise and layer-wise structural modulation aligned with RoPE-induced structure without modifying the pretrained backbone.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on mathematical and commonsense reasoning benchmarks across multiple backbone models reportedly show that DyPAM consistently outperforms strong existing PEFT baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: PEFT is presented as a standard approach for adapting large language models to downstream tasks.
Existing PEFT methods commonly use uniform and static adaptations despite structured heterogeneity in attention and positional representations.
The paper proposes DyPAM, which modulates positional attention through query and key representations using input-, dimension-, head-, and layer-wise adaptations.
The authors report consistent improvements over strong PEFT baselines across mathematical and commonsense reasoning benchmarks and multiple backbone models.

source_observation.claim: The method applies fine-grained modulation across input conditions, dimensions, heads, and layers.

interpretation.claim: Adaptation may benefit from matching the structural heterogeneity of the representation being tuned.

application.claim: When designing PEFT methods, consider structure-aware modulation rather than uniform parameter updates.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design is beneficial beyond the reported reasoning benchmarks and backbone models.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide benchmark names, quantitative results, or statistical comparisons.
The abstract does not specify the computational or parameter overhead of DyPAM.
The abstract does not describe ablations, limitations, or failure cases.
